problem_statement: The CoAP client cannot send a GET request to a multicast address and stream responses from multiple servers as described in RFC 7252 section 8. A request should be able to specify a multicast collection timeout and have its response callback invoked once per responding server (each callback carrying that server's unicast source address and length), followed by one final callback with a NULL source that signals no more responses will arrive for that request. A multicast request that is marked confirmable must be rejected as an error (multicast requests are always non-confirmable), a request that sets a multicast timeout for a unicast destination must be rejected, confirmable (CON) responses to a multicast request must be dropped instead of being acknowledged, and blockwise (Block1/Block2) responses in multicast mode must be dropped. Observe and multicast together must also be rejected.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/lib/coap_client -s tests/net/lib/coap_client/net.coap.client -s net.coap.client -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The statement describes the multicast feature well but omits three names the tests rely on (CONFIG_COAP_CLIENT_MULTICAST, multicast_timeout_ms, source_len) and does not specify the exact error code (-EINVAL) for the confirmable-rejection case. All can be repaired by adding the names to the statement.

problems.detail: The Kconfig option CONFIG_COAP_CLIENT_MULTICAST is used by the test (add_compile_definitions) but the statement never names it; the agent cannot know what macro to gate the feature with.
The request struct field multicast_timeout_ms is used by the tests (req.multicast_timeout_ms = ...) but the statement only says 'a multicast collection timeout' without giving the field name.

The response data struct field source_len is used by the tests (data->source_len) but the statement only says 'length' without giving the exact field name. The field 'source' is implied by 'source address' in the statement, but 'length' is too generic to determine the name source_len.
The test test_multicast_confirmable_rejected checks for -EINVAL specifically, but the statement only says 'must be rejected as an error' without specifying which error code.

problem_statement_fixed: The CoAP client cannot send a GET request to a multicast address and stream responses from multiple servers as described in RFC 7252 section 8. This feature is gated by the Kconfig option CONFIG_COAP_CLIENT_MULTICAST. A request should be able to specify a multicast collection timeout via the multicast_timeout_ms field (in milliseconds) in the request struct, and have its response callback invoked once per responding server (each callback carrying that server's unicast source address in the source field and its length in the source_len field of the response data struct), followed by one final callback with a NULL source that signals no more responses will arrive for that request. A multicast request that is marked confirmable must be rejected with -EINVAL (multicast requests are always non-confirmable), a request that sets a multicast timeout for a unicast destination must be rejected with -EINVAL, confirmable (CON) responses to a multicast request must be dropped instead of being acknowledged, and blockwise (Block1/Block2) responses in multicast mode must be dropped. Observe and multicast together must also be rejected with -EINVAL.
